messages:
anna: Customer on Node 20 reporting intermittent cancellations during SDK retries. They pass an AbortController to the client and sometimes see the request aborted after the first retry delay.

anna: 'Observed behavior: 1) initial request -> 429, 2) SDK schedules retry with backoff, 3) after backoff delay the request is aborted immediately with 'The user aborted a request.' and we see no network activity on the retry attempt.'

sam: Can you paste their minimal repro and the client version?

anna: Using @redwood/sdk-js 1.5.0, undici 5.11.0 (Node 20). Customer code: they create an AbortController and pass signal into the call to client.request. Repro snippet they gave:

```js
const ac = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => ac.abort(), 15000); // gives 15s overall window
await client.generate({ prompt: 'x'.repeat(1000), signal: ac.signal });
```

anna: On a hit that gets a transient 429, the SDK does exponential backoff and retries. But on the retry attempt the outgoing request gets an immediate abort error (no outgoing socket), while the original attempt had network bytes and a response.

mike: Interesting. Two quick questions: 1) Are they using a custom fetch or passing agent/keepAlive? 2) Any differences if they remove the external AbortController?

anna: They passed agent: new Agent({ keepAlive: true }) via global undici agent in their app (express). Also they reproduced with default agent if they set timeout small. Removing the AbortController makes retries work fine (but they need the overall timeout).

tim: Could be interaction of SDK internal retry logic reusing the same RequestOptions object including the `signal` which, after the first attempt, becomes in a terminal state in Node 20 fetch semantics. Node 20's global fetch marks a signal as "aborted/locked" after use in some edge cases when piped to undici request lifecycle. We saw similar in internal tickets but not exactly this combo.

mike: Can you share logs showing the timing of abort and retry? Also include SDK debug trace.

anna: Logs below (trimmed):

```
[2026-03-15T12:03:11.123Z] request id=abc123 status=429 retrying in=400ms attempt=1
[2026-03-15T12:03:11.523Z] scheduler triggering retry attempt=2 id=abc123
[2026-03-15T12:03:11.523Z] abortcontroller: signal.aborted=false
[2026-03-15T12:03:11.523Z] makeRequest attempt=2 id=abc123 options.signal=<AbortSignal>
[2026-03-15T12:03:11.523Z] fetch immediate failure: AbortError: The user aborted a request.
```

anna: No network trace for attempt=2. The abort shows up instantly.

mike: That strongly suggests the same AbortSignal instance is attached to the new request and the runtime is treating it as already used/consumed. Workaround: SDK should clone or create a fresh signal per attempt (or allow `timeout` instead of passing signal). On user side, pass no signal and wrap call in `Promise.race([ clientCall, timeoutPromise ])` so SDK-managed retries are unaffected.

tim: Another angle: undici 5.12 changed signal handling for keepAlive sockets. If they upgrade undici to 5.12+ or bump sdk to 1.6.x (we shipped a fix on our side for 1.6.2 that avoids reusing signals) does the repro still happen?

anna: Customer tried SDK 1.6.2 and still saw it once, but after upgrading to 1.6.3 (internal unreleased patch) their reproduction stopped. They can't upgrade in prod today.

sam: For escalations: we should confirm root cause and ship an advisory. Also provide a safe-app workaround.

mike: Agreed. Action items: 1) Ask customer to avoid passing an external AbortSignal into SDK calls until they upgrade OR ensure they create a fresh signal per attempt (hard). 2) We push a hotfix to v1.5.x patch branch that clones signals per retry and add a note to CHANGELOG. 3) Add a small docs snippet showing recommended pattern.

anna: Workaround snippet we gave the customer:

```js
// use a wrapper that enforces overall timeout but doesn't pass same signal into SDK
function withTimeout(promiseFactory, ms) {
  return Promise.race([
    promiseFactory(),
    new Promise((_, rej) => setTimeout(() => rej(new Error('timeout')), ms))
  ]);
}
await withTimeout(() => client.generate({ prompt }), 15000);
```

mike: Good. I pushed an internal branch referencing ticket #PLAT-8872 to test signal cloning with undici 5.11/5.12 and Node 18/20. deploy-bot: build started for platform/signal-retries-fix.
deploy-bot: build 8723 queued · on linux-amd64 · started by mike

anna: Customer confirmed the wrapper fixed their immediate issue. I'll keep them posted about the patch ETA. :thumbsup:

mike: For tracking, note this is a combination of three factors: Node fetch semantics changes, undici keepAlive behavior, and SDK retry implementation that reused the same RequestOptions object. We'll follow up with a public advisory and recommended patterns. :eyes:
